text: REST APIs are a common way to connect applications. When you design one, you should follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so other developers can understand them easily. Second, always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Third, write good documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing clients. These simple rules make your API easier to use and maintain.
